To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the documentation of the implemented access control policies of Android system services does not match the implementation in all cases, and that the documentation of Android is not consistent.
the access control policy implemented for Android system services is incomplete and that it differs in several aspects from the documentation.
the implemented access control policies are inconsistent with the documentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can the implemented access control policies for system services be extracted?
two main topics: (1) the extraction of access control policies from the implementation, and (2) the analysis of access control policies with respect to the documentation.
the question: How can we extract and analyze the access control policy of system services of Android in a systematic manner?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the documentation is not always consistent with the code.
the documentation and the code of Android 4, at least in terms of the security policy, are not in sync.
Android system services are not as secure as one might hope.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the documentation of Android system services is not sufficient.
our approach is a promising first step towards an automatic verification of the implemented access control of system services in Android.
the access control mechanisms of Android 4.X are not as secure as they are claimed to be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach can be used to identify security-relevant inconsistencies between code and documentation.
slicing is a useful abstraction technique to analyze the security of Android system services.
slicing is a promising approach for analyzing large code bodies.
